stem: If f(x) = 4e^x − 2cos x, what is f′(π/2)?

rationales.A: This combines two errors. It treats e^x like a power function (4·(π/2)·e^(π/2 − 1) = 2πe^(π/2 − 1)) and it drops the cosine term, which contributes +2. The derivative of e^x is e^x, so the first term is 4e^(π/2), and the full answer is 4e^(π/2) + 2.
rationales.B: This uses (cos x)′ = sin x instead of −sin x. The correct derivative is 4e^x − 2(−sin x) = 4e^x + 2sin x, giving 4e^(π/2) + 2.
rationales.D: This uses (cos x)′ = −cos x, so the cosine term becomes +2cos(π/2) = 0. The derivative of cos x is −sin x, so that term contributes +2sin(π/2) = 2 and f′(π/2) = 4e^(π/2) + 2.

title: Derivative of e^x and cos x
